question: Pilocarpine reduce the intraocular pressure in persons with closed angle glaucoma by:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Pilocarpine" -> "stimulates muscarinic receptors" -> "contracts iris sphincter muscle" -> "increases space in anterior chamber" -> "enhances aqueous humor outflow" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Pilocarpine" -> "activates ciliary muscle" -> "facilitates aqueous humor drainage" -> "reduces intraocular pressure" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Pilocarpine" -> "induces miosis" -> "opens trabecular meshwork" -> "increases aqueous humor outflow" -> "lowers intraocular pressure" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Pilocarpine" -> "causes contraction of iris sphincter" -> "reduces angle closure" -> "improves aqueous humor drainage" -> "decreases intraocular pressure" -> 75%
analysis: Pilocarpine is a muscarinic agonist that primarily works by contracting the iris sphincter muscle, which leads to miosis (pupil constriction). This action helps to open the angle between the iris and cornea, facilitating increased aqueous humor outflow and thereby reducing intraocular pressure in closed angle glaucoma. While it does increase aqueous humor outflow, the primary mechanism in this context is the contraction of the iris sphincter muscle.
